stateOfPlay: The lists closed on 8 September and six polls landed on the 9th. None of them moves the blocs much — Kantar has the Netanyahu bloc on 52 and Eisenkot's side on 56 once Hendel is counted — but underneath, the thing that decides this election has moved a great deal. Four of the six now put Yoaz Hendel's Reservists below the 3.25% threshold, and Hendel is the partner the change bloc's only majority ran through. Without him Eisenkot reaches 55, and even reaching for Ra'am leaves him at 60. So the threshold is still where this is settled, but it has stopped being only about Ofer Winter. On Kantar's numbers, Winter and Smotrich both missing would put a Zionist coalition on exactly 61 with no Ra'am in it — while the same arithmetic that rewards Eisenkot when the small parties of the right fail punishes him when his own does. Nobody is close to governing, and the margin now runs through four parties who may not be in the Knesset at all.
raamNote: Ra'am is the hinge, and the change bloc is split on it. Eisenkot will not seat it in a cabinet but is preparing a minority government that leans on it from outside; Bennett has ruled out a repeat 'post-October 7'; Lieberman has ruled out both. Only Yair Golan is unequivocal. Those pledges have broken before — Bennett signed one on live television in 2021 and brought Ra'am into government months later — and Yoav Segelovich, a former Yesh Atid MK, now runs on Ra'am's list as the first Jewish figure to do so.
_outlooksComment: Odds are YOUR editorial call — these are a starting point, not a calculation. The seat totals beside each are computed live from polls.json.

outlooks.label: An Eisenkot government, minority or majority
outlooks.why: The core reaches {zionist} and crosses nobody's red line. From there it goes one of two ways: Ra'am joins and it clears 61, or it governs as a minority with Arab support from outside, which is what Eisenkot has been preparing for. The second needs no one to break a promise — only for Ra'am to abstain or back it in a confidence vote.

outlooks.label: Another stalemate
outlooks.why: The Netanyahu bloc tops out at {net} even with Winter, and has no further seat available to it that is not Arab-majority. If the change bloc also cannot settle on Ra'am — inside the coalition or outside it — nobody forms a government and Israel votes again.

outlooks.label: Netanyahu returns
outlooks.why: It falls short, and needs Hendel to abandon the draft red line his party was founded on. The likelier route is not this coalition but a different field: Religious Zionism holding its seats, Amcha Yisrael clearing the threshold rather than splitting the right, and a seat or two moving back from Yashar.

wildCardNote: The wild card is Yoaz Hendel's The Reservists — the one partner outside the change bloc who can join it without crossing anybody's stated red line, and the reason its only majority exists. Four of the six polls taken on 9 September put the party below the threshold. Its refusal to sit with the ultra-Orthodox over the draft closes off the right, so if it clears it decides the government, and if it fails it takes Eisenkot's margin with it.
_presetsComment: The 'Try a scenario' buttons. Editable here so the scenario list can follow the campaign without a design re-export. 'note' shows as a caveat when the scenario is loaded.

presets.label: Change bloc + Hendel
presets.note: Hendel is the one partner outside the bloc who can join it without crossing anybody's stated red line — which is why whether his party clears the threshold decides so much.

presets.label: Change bloc + Ra'am
presets.note: It crosses two declared refusals: Bennett has ruled out a repeat 'post-October 7', and Lieberman has ruled out relying on Ra'am at all. Only Eisenkot and Golan are open to it.

presets.label: Current government + Winter
presets.note: The Netanyahu bloc at its ceiling, {net}. There is no further seat available to it that is not Arab-majority, which is why Winter's seats do not solve the problem Netanyahu warned they would create.

_thresholdComment: The 'if they miss' buttons. `drop` lists the parties that fail to clear 3.25%; their votes are redistributed and the whole board recomputes, so the notes stay qualitative and the numbers come from the live poll.

thresholdScenarios.label: Everyone clears
thresholdScenarios.note: Netanyahu {net}, the change bloc {change}, {zionist} once Hendel joins. Whether that is enough depends on the poll — and beyond it the only seats left are Ra'am's, which Bennett and Lieberman have both ruled out relying on.

thresholdScenarios.label: Winter misses
thresholdScenarios.note: Winter's votes redistribute: the Netanyahu bloc lands on {net}, Eisenkot's side on {zionist} with Hendel. Netanyahu warned his own camp about exactly this.

thresholdScenarios.label: Smotrich misses
thresholdScenarios.note: Religious Zionism has been shown at zero by several pollsters. Losing it puts the Netanyahu bloc on {net} against {zionist} — and costs him more than losing Winter does.

thresholdScenarios.label: Winter and Smotrich miss
thresholdScenarios.note: The Netanyahu bloc collapses to {net}, and a Zionist coalition with no Ra'am in it reaches {zionist}. The best case available to Eisenkot.

thresholdScenarios.label: Hendel misses
thresholdScenarios.note: Barely moves the blocs — {net} against {change} — but it takes away the four seats that were Eisenkot's margin, and even reaching for Ra'am only gets him to {withRaam}.

thresholdScenarios.label: Ra'am misses
thresholdScenarios.note: Ra'am's seats redistribute and Eisenkot's Zionist total rises to {zionist}, while Netanyahu lands on {net}. The route that ran through Ra'am is simply gone.
